title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes, which continue La Longue Marche. There Grothendieck studies profinite completions of groups attached to the Teichmüller tower in low dimension, apparently around the elliptic points rho and sigma of M_{1,1}, i.e. j = 0 and j = 1728.
- M is a profinite group (by the next page, M = M(0)·S^{+^}, with M(0) ≃ M_{0,3}(0)).
- N_rho^* = Norm_M(L_rho) is the normaliser of a local subgroup L_rho attached to the special point rho.
- Gothic G (transcribed as 𝔖) is an auxiliary group with normal subgroups G ⊃ G^+ ⊃ Π ⊃ Π_0.
- mu = Z/2, and S_3 is the symmetric group.

What the previous page was trying to do. It tried to show that the homomorphism N_rho^* → G/Π_0 factors through N_rho^*/M^0(-J). It then tried to bound the kernel using the fact that D_rho embeds, so that D_rho has index ≤ 2. That argument stalled on identifying the character M''^! → mu with epsilon_3.

The proposition ('Je vois mieux'). Compare two filtrations.
- G/Π_0 is filtered with successive quotients G/G^+ ≃ mu, G^+/Π ≃ S_3 and Π/Π_0 ≃ mu. Its order is therefore 2·6·2 = 24.
- M is filtered by M ⊃ M'' ⊃ M''^! ⊃ M^{0!}, with quotients M/M'' ≃ mu via epsilon_2, M''/M''^! ≃ S_3, and M''^!/M^{0!} ≃ mu via epsilon_3.
- Claim: the canonical map M → G/Π_0 respects the filtrations and induces the obvious isomorphisms on the graded pieces.
- Consequence: by induction with the five lemma, M → G/Π_0 is surjective with kernel exactly M^{0!}. So G/Π_0 is a quotient of M of order 24.

Application.
- Admitting the proposition, Ker(N_rho^* → G/Π_0) = N_rho^* ∩ M^{0!}.
- Using the earlier computation N_rho ∩ M_0^! = Z_rho^! = M'(-J), and intersecting with M'', the kernel is M'(-J) ∩ M'' = M^0(-J).
- Hence the induced map (4σ), N_rho^*/M^0(-J) → G/Π_0, is injective.
- The next page concludes that both groups have order 24, so (4σ) is an isomorphism.

What it serves. The result identifies the finite 'local' quotient of the normaliser of the elliptic-point subgroup in the profinite group M with an explicit order-24 group. This feeds into part d), the structure of M_{rho,sigma} = N_rho^* ×_Γ N_sigma^* ×_Γ G_{rho,sigma} and a homomorphism M → M_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho. That is part of a description of the profinite Teichmüller group of genus 1 (or of M_{0,4}) as an amalgam over its elliptic points, with Γ ≃ the arithmetic group (Π_Q~ in the notes, presumably Gal(Q̄/Q) or its GT-type substitute).
errors: The proposition is explicitly 'admitted' (Admettant ce point), not proved on this page. The compatibility of M → G/Π_0 with the filtrations, and in particular the identification of the induced character M''^! → mu with epsilon_3, is the very point left open on the previous page.

The notation drifts: M^{0!} versus M_0^!, and N_rho versus N_rho^*. The step 'N_rho^* ∩ M^{0!} = M'(-J) ∩ M''' silently uses N_rho^* ∩ M_0^! = Z_rho^! = M'(-J) together with M^{0!} = M_0^! ∩ M''. This is plausible but not justified here.
The final isomorphism needs the order of N_rho^*/M^0(-J) to be 24. That is asserted on the next page and not checked on this page.

ideas.what: Identifying a finite quotient of a profinite (mapping-class/Teichmüller-type) group by comparing two filtrations with isomorphic graded pieces mu, S_3, mu. The kernel of M → G/Π_0 is the last filtration step.
ideas.modern_name: Filtration / graded comparison (five-lemma argument); finite quotients of profinite mapping class groups of order 24

ideas.what: Computing the quotient N_rho^*/M^0(-J) of the normaliser of the local (elliptic point) subgroup and showing it embeds into, hence is isomorphic to, an order-24 group. This serves an amalgam description M_{rho,sigma} of the profinite Teichmüller group over its two elliptic points.
ideas.modern_name: Local structure at elliptic points of M_{1,1} / finite-order elements and their normalisers in profinite SL_2(Z) or Γ_{1,1}, as used in GT-hat and Lochak–Schneps type 'local' conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura (profinite GT and the genus 0/1 Teichmüller tower, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Continuation of La Longue Marche (1981), unpublished. Only the program is described in Esquisse d'un programme.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical lemma inside a long computation. It replaces a stalled index argument with a cleaner filtration comparison and concludes an isomorphism of order-24 groups. The overall programme (profinite Teichmüller tower at elliptic points) is known in spirit, and nothing on this page appears independently new.
transcription_corrections: The gothic letter is the same as on the previous page (𝔊, written G here), not 𝔖. Read 'filtration de 𝔊/Π_0 par 𝔊/𝔊^+ ≃ mu, 𝔊^+/Π ≃ 𝔖_3, et Π/Π_0 ≃ mu'.
Line 4 appears to read '𝔊^*/π_0^*' (with stars) in the image rather than '𝔖^*/Π_0'.
'Ker(N_rho^* → 𝔊/Π_0) = N_rho^* ∩ M_0^{!!}' carries a struck-through trailing symbol. The intended set is N_rho^* ∩ M^{0!}.

'Admettant ce point, on trouve donc' is correct. The line before (4σ) reads 'Donc [l'élément] on a bien un homom. injectif (4σ), et comme les groupes', continuing on the next page with '…en présence ont même ordre 24'.
